long.vo: The last over of the day. जसप्रीत बुमराह has the second new ball. He bowls an inswinger at Henry Nicholls' toes, and Nicholls jams his bat down just in time. Earlier that day, New Zealand were seventy for five. So how did India lose a day they were winning?

scene.kicker: BUMRAH'S LAST BALL OF THE DAY · OVER 81
sub: Nicholls jammed his bat down in time.

long.vo: Rewind to the toss. शुभमन गिल chose to bowl, and the pitch gave him every reason: fifteen millimetres of grass, and moisture on top. Everything you're about to hear comes from our ball-by-ball of the day.
long.chapter: Act one: the morning India owned

long.vo: Over one. बुमराह, full, on the fourth-stump line, the seam bolt upright. Tom Latham, sure it would leave, left it. It came back. Two for one, and the day had barely begun.

scene.title: Bowled.
scene.name: LATHAM b BUMRAH
scene.caption: Latham left it, expecting it to go away. It came back.

long.vo: बुमराह has been here before. In the first innings of the Wellington Test in twenty twenty, he took one wicket for eighty-eight, in twenty-six overs. This time, his first over had Latham.

foot: Bumrah, in the first innings of each Wellington Test.
OUR ARCHIVE (2020) · DAY 1 OF 2026 SO FAR

long.vo: Devon Conway lasted three more overs, and one review. He was given out caught behind, and the replay showed the noise came before the ball reached the bat. Not out. Then अंशुल कंबोज bowled the ball he'd been waiting for: full, angled in, seaming away. Conway edged. Twelve for two.

Then the luck swung back and forth. रचिन रवींद्र survived an edge India did not review, and a direct hit that missed. आकाश दीप got him anyway: extra bounce, short of a length. The next over, बुमराह's good-length nipbacker found Daryl Mitchell's inside edge, and यशस्वी जायसवाल took it at short leg. Fifty-two for four.

items.d: short of a length, extra bounce · 51/3
good-length nipbacker, inside edge to short leg · 52/4

long.vo: At lunch, sixty for four. New Zealand were playing and missing, or edging, at one ball in four. India had the match by the throat.

scene.label: OF BALLS DREW A FALSE SHOT · CRICBUZZ'S OWN FIGURE

long.vo: After lunch, बुमराह came back for one more. Tom Blundell, short of a length, angled in, left his bat hanging out, and गिल held on at first slip. Seventy for five, in twenty-eight overs. If you had stopped watching here, you would have called it India's day. Hold on to that number.

head.t: WHERE THE FIVE WICKETS CAME FROM

long.vo: And India had got their length right. Look at what worked: two hundred and two balls on a good length, one point four eight an over, three wickets. The full balls took two but cost over five an over. The short balls cost nearly four, and took none.

head.sub: INDIA'S SEAMERS · RUNS PER OVER BY LENGTH · CRICBUZZ'S TABLE

long.vo: Act two. The hour it slipped away.
long.chapter: Act two: the hour it slipped

long.vo: Over thirty. बुमराह nips one back at Glenn Phillips, who is on six. गिल reviews the lbw. The third umpire sees a spike: an inside edge. India lose the review. Five overs later, another inside edge rolls past the stumps. Phillips is still there, and so is Henry Nicholls.

long.vo: Then the sun came out. At lunch the pitch report said it was browning off, with not the kind of movement we saw before lunch. The numbers agree. Cricbuzz has false shots down from twenty-five per cent before lunch to fourteen after. On good-length balls, the same ball that drew thirty per cent false shots now drew thirteen.

head.sub: FALSE SHOTS · CRICBUZZ · AFTER-LUNCH SPLIT DERIVED

long.vo: The pitch had changed, and India's lengths changed with it, the wrong way. Short balls went from nineteen per cent of their seam deliveries before lunch to thirty-six after. The pitch report said India could have been fuller.

head.sub: SHARE OF SEAM BALLS · DERIVED FROM CRICBUZZ'S TABLES

long.vo: And the ball itself. The new ball did the damage: three wickets for fifty-two in twenty overs. Over the next sixty, the old ball took two more, and cost a hundred and eighty-four runs.

head.sub: NEW ZEALAND'S RUNS AND WICKETS BY AGE OF THE BALL

long.vo: Act three. The stand that would not break.

Henry Nicholls played the innings his record promised. A hundred and thirteen not out, off two hundred and twenty-one balls, his fifth Test hundred at the Basin Reserve. In our archive, he had four here before today. Playing late, behind the line. Cricbuzz had his control at ninety per cent.

scene.label: OFF 221 BALLS · 14 FOURS · CONTROL 90%
scene.note: fifth Test hundred at the Basin Reserve

long.vo: With Glenn Phillips, ninety-four not out, he built a stand of one hundred and seventy-three. Fifty-four singles. Seven twos. Seven threes. Twenty-one fours. Seventy-three per cent of the balls were dots, but they never let India settle.
Put the whole day on one strip. Five wickets in the first twenty-eight overs. None in the next fifty-three.

head.t: THE WHOLE DAY, OVER BY OVER
head.sub: RUNS IN EACH OVER · RED = WICKET · GREEN = MAIDEN

scene.footnote: OUR BALL-BY-BALL · LUNCH AFTER 22.5 OVERS, TEA AFTER 47.6

long.vo: The bowlers. बुमराह, three for fifty-two, and in the forty-eight balls after Blundell, thirty-five runs and no wicket. आकाश दीप, one for thirty-three. वॉशिंगटन सुंदर, none for thirty-eight in sixteen overs. कंबोज, one for fifty-seven. प्रसिद्ध कृष्णा, none for fifty-eight, with nine fours.

India also dropped a chance. Nicholls, on a hundred and two, top-edged a pull, and पंत and पडिक्कल both stopped, each waiting for the other. At eighty overs, India took the second new ball. बुमराह's first ball went for four. Then five dots, the last one that toe-crusher. Nicholls jammed his bat down just in time. Two hundred and forty-three for five. That is the ball we started with.

So who won day one? New Zealand, the sun, and a catch nobody took. India's reply is on day two. As Cricbuzz's commentators said at tea, anything over two hundred and fifty could hurt India later, and that is only fifty runs away. Your call: who won day one? Nicholls, Phillips, or बुमराह? Comment one, two or three, and tell us what India should do first.

long.description:
India vs New Zealand, 1st Test day one analysis at the Basin Reserve, Wellington (19 November 2026): how 70 for 5 became 243 for 5. Where India's five wickets came from (line, length and movement), why the pitch eased as the sun came out, how India's lengths drifted shorter after lunch, and the unbroken 173 between Henry Nicholls (113*) and Glenn Phillips (94*).

YOUR CALL: who won day one? Comment 1 (Nicholls), 2 (Phillips) or 3 (Bumrah), and tell us what India should do first on day two.

Method: our ball-by-ball of the day (Cricbuzz commentary); Cricbuzz's own session tables for control, false-shot and length figures, with the after-lunch splits derived by subtracting the lunch table from the day table. Placement of the wicket balls is read from the commentary and is illustrative.
